commits.subject: fix(ghidra): keep the cross-format branch callee multi-block
commits.body:
fix(ghidra): keep the cross-format branch callee multi-block

The cross-format oracle requires a callee whose recovered control flow
has more than one basic block, and rea_cross_branch provided it through
a symmetric if/else of tail calls. Clang 21 folds that shape into a
conditional negate plus one tail branch, a single basic block, so the
lane rejected a correct Ghidra analysis of the fixture.

Give the branch a loop whose trip count depends on a volatile global:
no compiler can eliminate the backedge, and the callee stays multi-block
at every optimization level on every toolchain.

Electron recognition matched callee spellings, so a bundler rename such as

commits.body:
fix(javascript): stop replaying earlier writes for each object property write

Repeated property writes to one object made member-mutation collection
cubic. Each write evaluated its target binding to rule out a primitive,
and every evaluation folded all earlier mutation paths, copying every
slot once per path. 2,000 writes to one object took 27 s and 4,000 took
203 s.

- A recorded write always leaves a non-primitive binding value, so only
  the first write to a binding needs the primitive check.
- Apply mutation paths per slot in one pass with the same ordering
  semantics instead of one full slot copy per path.

Inventory paired every path under one case spelling with every path under

commits.subject: fix(apple): bound binary plist expansion before decoding keyed archives (#1515)
commits.body:
fix(apple): bound binary plist expansion before decoding keyed archives (#1515)

inspect_keyed_archive passed caller-selected binary plists straight to
plist.parseBinary, which recurses on every object reference and copies
shared containers. A 484-byte archive of forty nested [next, next] arrays
grew the process past 4 GB until it died with no result, which would also
end an MCP server. A 125-byte self-referencing array overflowed the stack
and was reported as an artifact too large to process.

The iterative reference walk that already guards decode_interface_builder
now runs first, with an 8x keyed-archive decode budget. Over-budget depth
or expansion is a limit; a reference cycle is a malformed archive. Its
"decoder" bounds admit the same layouts plist.parseBinary reads, so
accepted archives stay accepted. Interface Builder behavior is unchanged.

fix(javascript): expand an escaped receiver's methods once (#1495) (#1517)

Since #1471, escaping an object also escapes every method's results. Each
call through the object escapes it as the receiver, and each escape

and path collapse to one, because the escape walk treats them alike.

fix(ida): canonicalize the headless workspace root before opening (#1481)

On macOS the default workspace root is os.tmpdir() under /var/folders,
and /var is a symlink to /private/var. idalib-mcp reports the canonical
input path from idb_open/idb_list, while REA compared it against the
uncanonicalized private copy with normalize(), so every headless IDA
analysis failed its identity check (surfacing as unreadable_output) and
the spawned idalib worker was never released.

Resolve the workspace root with realpath() when allocating the private
workspace so the input path REA sends already matches what upstream
reports.

Add a read-only ADB device-acquisition family over the caller's adb binary:
inspect_adb_client, list_adb_devices, inspect_adb_device, list_adb_packages,
and pull_adb_package, exposed through the CLI and MCP with shared admission,

recorded when observed.

emulator: full 224-package inventory, a real two-APK split set pulled with
byte-exact digests, and a 73.9 MB system-package pull. npm run verify:adb
records the lane; parser goldens come from the same device. READMEs carry
the new row in every supported language.

* feat(adb): complete the adb surface with observation, transfer, and lifecycle tools

Extend the ADB family from five to twenty-four operations, all through
fixed adb argument vectors with no shell exposure:

Observation: read_adb_logcat (bounded dump, count/buffer/pid), inspect_adb_package
(dumpsys package projection), list_adb_processes (ps -A), list_adb_directory

verification, explicit overwrite authority), resolve_adb_packages (substring

Lifecycle for dynamic analysis, each declaring mutatesTarget:

start_adb_activity (typed extras as --es/--ez/--ei/--el/--ef), and stop_adb_app

commits.subject: fix(electron): support packaged app.asar pages and rewritten unpacked companions (#1400)
commits.body:
fix(electron): support packaged app.asar pages and rewritten unpacked companions (#1400)

* fix(electron): resolve pages served from inside app.asar

Packaged Electron applications load their renderer pages from file URLs
inside app.asar. The host filesystem cannot stat those paths, so
list_electron_targets excluded every such page as unsupported_url and
inspect_electron_page could not select it.

Resolve these URLs the way Electron's file protocol does: the first .asar
path component that is a regular file is the archive, and the remainder
must name a regular file in its header. Directories, links, and missing
members stay rejected. Parsed headers are cached by archive identity.

* fix(artifacts): extract and explain rewritten ASAR unpacked companions

Packaging tools commonly sign or strip .asar.unpacked native binaries after
writing the archive header, so their declared hashes no longer match.
analyze_javascript_application already accepts integrity_policy, but
extract_artifact did not, and inspect_artifact and extract_artifact still
told callers to "get a fresh copy", which cannot help for a shipped app.

- Accept integrity_policy on extract_artifact (MCP and CLI). The default
  still fails closed; record-and-continue writes the observed bytes and
  returns the extracted files' integrity_contradictions records.
- Name the unpacked entry and the post-packaging cause in integrity
  failures, and point every operation that accepts integrity_policy at
  record-and-continue.
- Report an active unpacked entry whose companion file is absent as
  unavailable with its logical path instead of a format failure.
- Share one integrity_policy schema across the inventory, extraction, and
  JavaScript application inputs.

* fix(electron): bound ASAR headers before allocation

* feat(jeb): add JEB engine provider over its MCP interface

Add a bring-your-own JEB provider that serves project, unit, and
decompilation inspection from a caller-started JEB client speaking MCP
(streamable HTTP, selected with REA_JEB_MCP_URL). Expose four provider-neutral
operations through shared CLI/MCP workflows: inspect_jeb_client,
open_jeb_project, list_jeb_units, and decompile_jeb_item, each returning
Evidence with engine identity, endpoint, and preserved refusal reasons.

The adapter keeps JEB's envelope semantics: success fields are parsed
format-aware at the boundary, message-only refusals become unsupported-target
errors with the engine's own reason, transport failures become availability
failures with recovery guidance, and unit pagination derives coverage from the
engine's 100-item page cap. Explicit unknowns (implicitly selected unit,
omitted filters) are reported instead of guessed.

Verified against a real JEB 5.48.0 licensed build serving jeb-mcp-server 1.3.0
headless: client inspection, unit listing, and method decompilation were
exercised through the CLI, MCP boundary, and scripts/verify-jeb.mjs.
JEB 5.48.0 headless instances do not advertise open_project; the refusal is
preserved and documented.

* fix(jeb): verify against a real signed APK and fix CLI option surface

Verify the provider against a locally built, v1/v2/v3-signed probe APK
(binary manifest, classes.dex with a launcher activity) on JEB 5.48.0: the
full unit tree (apk, manifest, three certificate units, dex bytecode,
decompiler), wildcard-filtered and paginated unit listing with derived
coverage, parent-restricted listing, and launcher-activity method
decompilation through both CLI and MCP, including dexdec's inline
constant folding of the probe's obfuscated tag.

Move list-jeb-units filter/pagination and decompile-jeb-item unit selection
from positional arguments to options; the MCP schemas are unchanged.

* fix(jeb): preserve engine refusals through the real MCP boundary

Testing against the published Signal 8.30.3 universal APK exposed a boundary
bug the scripted provider tests missed: decodeJebToolResult raised a protocol
error for isError results before the provider could map JEB's
{success:false, message} envelope, so real engine refusals surfaced as
unreadable output instead of the engine's own reason. Decode refusal
envelopes like any structured result and let the provider preserve the
reason; cover the decoder directly, including contentless and unparseable
results.

Signal verification: full 109 MB R8/Kotlin/Compose APK with four signature
schemes and native arm64 ELF units parsed; MainActivity.onCreate and R8
synthetic lambdas decompiled through CLI and MCP; paginated, filtered, and
parent-restricted unit listing; refusal path confirmed on the live engine.

(112 MB): per-ABI libapp.so Dart AOT snapshot images analyzed as native code
with 75k methods on arm64, snapshot internals and wrapper methods decompiled
through both CLI and MCP with explicit unit selection, decoded manifest, and
filtered native-library unit discovery. Note that JEB 5.48.0 headless does
not expose the dedicated Dart snapshot processor or run_script; both remain

fix(javascript): recover Electron APIs through default imports and optional calls (#1673)

`import electron from "electron"` bound the module with a leading `default`
export segment, so `electron.ipcMain.handle(...)`, `new
electron.BrowserWindow(...)` and destructuring from that binding matched no
Electron API. Electron's CommonJS exports define no `default` member, so the
segment can only denote the module object; drop it when classifying
Electron bindings.

The binding classifier already recorded optional-call roots, but the IPC,
context-bridge, utility-process and sender-validation visitors accepted only
plain calls. `ipcMain?.handle(...)`, `contextBridge?.exposeInMainWorld(...)`
and the common `event.senderFrame?.url.startsWith(...)` check were dropped

ci: select semantic tests and fixture lanes for their guarded inputs (#1675)

Edits to `release.yml` or `real-ghidra-windows.yml` selected only the
workflow lane, so the shards holding releaseWorkflow, releaseCheckpoint
and realGhidraWindowsWorkflow tests were skipped. Actionlint checks
syntax only, so a PR could drop the package-before-publish gate, the
registry canary or the default-branch-only self-hosted runner restriction
without CI noticing.

Conformance fixture sources under tests/ set only the code lane, so the
conformance-fixtures and reconstruction-readiness jobs, the only callers
of `verify:fixtures` and `verify:readiness`, never ran for them. Route
the directories that build-conformance-fixtures.mjs compiles to both
lanes, and readiness applications to the readiness lane.

Both were raised by the Codex review of #1660 after it merged.

commits.subject: fix(native): bound PE resource RVAs by section virtual size (#1678)
commits.body:
fix(native): bound PE resource RVAs by section virtual size (#1678)

The PE resource reader treated each section as covering
`max(VirtualSize, SizeOfRawData)` bytes, the mapping #1596 removed from
managed RVA reads. A resource payload in the raw alignment padding past
VirtualSize was reported with a hash of bytes the image loader never maps.
A later section whose virtual range starts inside that padding was refused
as an overlapping mapping.

Containment and overlap now use the loader's virtual extent: VirtualSize,
or SizeOfRawData when VirtualSize is zero. Ranges must still be file-backed.

Refs #1596

commits.subject: fix(native): bind NativeAOT metadata to declared PE section extents
commits.body:
fix(native): bind NativeAOT metadata to declared PE section extents

Section headers distinguish the declared virtual extent from the on-disk raw extent, which may include alignment padding. Resource RVA ownership and overlap use VirtualSize, falling back to SizeOfRawData when VirtualSize is zero, and payload reads still require file-backed bytes.

The NativeAOT snapshot reader applies the same range rule to RVA reads, metadata scans, executable targets, and derived overlay bounds. Page-rounded loader mappings may expose tail bytes, but those bytes lie outside the declared section range used by these parsers.
